hero.subtitle: A fall at a Grand Avenue shop, an El Camino Real apartment complex, or anywhere in between can leave you with medical bills and unanswered questions. Our team handles premises liability cases and can review what happened to you, free of charge.

about.title: Arroyo Grande Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Slip and fall accidents in Arroyo Grande happen in ordinary places — a grocery store off E Grand Avenue, a rental unit near the Village, a parking lot along El Camino Real. What turns a bad fall into a legitimate claim is proof: a wet floor with no warning sign, broken pavement the property owner ignored, poor lighting on a stairwell. California law requires showing the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and did nothing about it. That's why documenting the scene matters as much as documenting your injury. We offer a free case review and can evaluate what happened, request surveillance footage before it's erased, and explain your options. You focus on healing; we'll help sort through the notice and liability questions with you.
commonInjuries: Wrist and arm fractures from bracing a fall
Torn ligaments or meniscus damage in the knee
Traumatic brain injury from a head strike
Shoulder dislocations and rotator cuff tears

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Premises Liability Claim

items.title: Proving the Owner Had Notice
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. We can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to build that case.

items.title: Preserving Video Before It's Gone
items.desc: Many stores and apartment complexes overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request that footage can be the difference between a supported claim and one with no visual evidence.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover even if you were partly responsible for the fall. We can help make sure any shared blame doesn't unfairly reduce what you're owed.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Arroyo Grande?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a city sidewalk or public building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's worth having us check the property owner's status quickly.

items.question: What if the store or landlord says they didn't know about the hazard?
items.answer: That's often where these cases are won or lost. Evidence like prior customer complaints, cleaning schedules, or how long the hazard existed can show the owner should have known. We can help track down that evidence before it disappears.

items.question: I fell at a business near US-101 in Arroyo Grande — does that change anything?
items.answer: Not necessarily, but busy commercial corridors like US-101 or E Grand Avenue often have larger retailers with formal incident-reporting systems and camera coverage. That can actually help your case if the footage and reports are requested promptly. We can help make sure that documentation is preserved rather than routinely deleted.
